stages.title: Alphabet, pronunciation, tooling
stages.goal: Read the alphabet fluently, pick a pronunciation, set up tools.
ready_when: You can name and write all 24 letters from memory
You can read the diacritics — breathings, accents, iota subscript — without stopping
STEP Bible and Logeion are bookmarked

parallel.title: Decide once: pronunciation
parallel.body: Erasmian is historically inaccurate but is what nearly every free video course uses; restored Koine is closer to first-century sound. Neither affects grammar. Default: Erasmian.

stages.note: Everything in Stage 0 is free. Paid items begin at Stage 1.

stages.title: Reading in earnest
stages.goal: Sustained reading of real NT Greek, references introduced.
ready_when: You can read a chapter of 1 John or Mark with the reader's edition at conversational pace
You understand what a footnote or apparatus marker is pointing at, even if you can't resolve it yourself

parallel.title: The Text of the New Testament
parallel.meta: Metzger & Ehrman · T1 · standard TC survey
parallel.body: Read this now, before the apparatus work of Stage 3 — alongside an intro-textbook spine (Ehrman or Powell) and Keener as a verse-by-verse background companion.

stages.note: Reading order: 1 John → Mark → John → shorter Pauline letters (Philippians, 1 Thessalonians).

stages.title: Apparatus, discourse, LXX
stages.goal: Read with the apparatus, not just the running text; broaden into aspect/discourse theory and the LXX.
ready_when: You read a UBS5/NA28 footnote and know what question it's answering before consulting Metzger
You can explain why a translation committee chose a reading, in claim-ladder terms

parallel.title: The CBGM
parallel.meta: concept note · the field's current genealogical method
parallel.body: Work the methodological fault line: CBGM, reasoned eclecticism, Byzantine priority — and the disputed-passage checklist (Mark 16, John 7:53–8:11, 1 John 5:7).

stages.note: No fixed end. Pick a variant from your current reading and look up why the committee decided as it did.

plan.title: Alphabet chunk 1 — α β γ δ ε ζ η θ
plan.detail: Names and sounds, Erasmian. Use Mounce BBG ch. 1 or the alphabet-and-diacritics note as your reference table.

plan.title: Alphabet chunk 2 — ι κ λ μ ν ξ ο π
plan.detail: Say each one aloud as you go.

plan.title: Alphabet chunk 3 — ρ σ/ς τ υ φ χ ψ ω
plan.detail: Full alphabet review: uppercase, lowercase, and final sigma.

plan.title: Breathings and the iota subscript
plan.detail: Smooth vs. rough breathing, then the iota subscript. Practice on five real NT words.

plan.title: The three accents — acute, grave, circumflex
plan.detail: What they mark, and why you can mostly ignore them for now — pitch, not stress, in the historical system.

plan.title: Read the whole alphabet aloud from memory
plan.detail: Uppercase and lowercase, timed. Repeat until you are under 60 seconds.

plan.title: First Daily Dose of Greek video — start the habit
plan.detail: Pick any verse from the archive. The point is the habit, not comprehension.

plan.title: NT201 Lecture 1 — “The Greek Language”
plan.detail: Alphabet, pronunciation, and a grammar overview.

plan.title: NT201 Lecture 3 — “The Alphabet and Pronunciation”
plan.detail: Gamma nasals, vowels, diphthongs, and breathing marks in more depth.

plan.title: Transcribe 1 John 1:1 by hand, letter by letter
plan.detail: From a printed or on-screen Greek text — slow, deliberate, no typing.

plan.title: Second Daily Dose of Greek video
plan.detail: Note any letters or sounds still shaky, then drill those specifically.

plan.title: Hover-parse every word of 1 John 1:1–4
plan.detail: Open STEP Bible and just look — don't try to memorize the grammar terms yet.

plan.title: NT201 Lecture 4 — “Punctuation and Syllabification”
plan.detail: Then re-read your Day 10 transcription and check it against the syllable rules.

plan.title: Read 1 John 1:1–4 aloud, Erasmian
plan.detail: From the text you transcribed. This is decoding fluency, not comprehension.
